note:
This is a model paper built around one plotting engine and one table engine, and the census reads cleanly because almost every field has a single value. Forty-three measured regions resolve to 18 figure rows, 7 table rows and 18 exclusions, with nothing unaccounted.

The exclusions are the interesting half. Eleven of the paper's display equations are pasted images - (1) and (2) on p7, (3) and (4) on p8, (5), (6) and (7) on p11, (8) and (9) on p12, (11) on p13 and (12) on p14 - while equations (10) and (13) alone survive as vector text. That asymmetry is the same detector artefact recorded on three earlier papers in this batch (MathType on P-A-2018-76082, NetLogo on P-F-2017-68940, pasted LaTeX on P-A-2018-76271), and it is worth folding into the lane findings: display mathematics pasted from an equation editor registers as artwork, one more region per equation, and the only defence is reading the crop. The twelfth exclusion is a pasted screenshot of the terrain-category bullet list on p14, and the last seven are the MATLAB code bands of Appendix B on pp27-32.

What the record calls a pattern. (1) Caption side is invariant: every exhibit in the paper, figure or table, prints its caption below the artwork. That is worth stating because the lane has now seen four conventions - side follows the exhibit kind, side follows the section of the paper, side follows the drawing tool, and here no convention at all beyond 'always below'. (2) The plot template is one export: joined traces, no markers, a key inside the top-right corner, no colour scale, no data labels, axes titled in words. The second sensitivity, legend position, is what identifies the single borrowed figure - its six-entry key sits below the x axis. (3) Panel count is a grammar: 1 for a curve family, 1x2 for a sweep over two parameters, 2x2 for the propagation process, 2x1 for the height sweep. (4) The table template is booktabs, seven times, with no shading, no merge, no diagonal, no note row and no continuation; the only two structural exceptions are Table 2's second header band and Table 4's two blocks, and Table 4's blocks are the paper's worst table defect because the headers are transposed against the columns beneath them.

What the record calls a defect. Figure 8's caption is stranded in the gutter between two plots and reads as captioned to the wrong one. Figure 16 names three F-layer altitudes in the prose and plots two. Figure 14's artwork carries MATLAB data-cursor tooltips burned in as if they were data labels. Table 5 calls a negative dBw entry a power. The p8 and p13 equations lose every superscript in the text layer ('m 3' for m^-3, 'dB=km' for dB/km). Figure 4 is announced two pages before it prints while every other exhibit is announced on its page or one page early.

How the section-level grammar runs. Sections 1 and 2 carry one exhibit each (the hop schematic and the notation glossary). Section 3 carries nine - one per mechanism as the model is derived: distribution of electron density, E-layer refraction, F-layer reflection, sea reflection, sea roughness, ground reflection, ground roughness times two, and background noise. Section 4 carries five, and the pattern there is tabulate-then-plot: Table 3 then Figure 11, Table 4 then (via Figure 12) Table 4, Table 5 then Figure 13. Sections 5 and 6 carry three, one of which is the appendix reprint. Section 7 carries three, all drawn with the same 2x2/2x1 grammar. Appendix A carries the two unnumbered reprints and Appendix B the code, which is excluded as not-an-exhibit.

Reading-order note. The caption of Figure 9 prints below Figure 9's panels, and Figure 8's caption prints immediately under Figure 8's single frame; the (a)/(b) labels under the Figure 9 panels belong to Figure 9, not to Figure 8, even though the text layer emits them in the order caption-8, label-a, label-b, caption-9.
rules: Caption side never varies and it inverts the usual table convention: all 18 figure captions and all 7 table captions print BELOW their artwork, so 25 of 25 exhibits are below-cased and the paper has no above-case to compare against [caption.position].

One numbering vocabulary runs the whole body - 'Figure N:' for 17 numbers and 'Table N:' for 6 - a colon with no period anywhere, and the only exhibits outside it are the two appendix reprints, which print no number at all [caption.numbering].

Captions are labels, not sentences: the 17 numbered figure captions run 8 to 41 words with a median of 18, and the four longest (Figures 5, 7, 11 and 14) are long only because they enumerate panels or parameter values rather than because they argue [caption.words].

Only three captions name a plotted symbol, and one of them names two: the 'change of s over grazing angle' of Figure 8, the 'change of s over frequency and Sh' of Figure 9 and the '... power with Sh' of Figure 13 - so everywhere else the caption names the exhibit's subject and leaves the plotted quantity to the axis title [caption.variable_count].

Units are stated in 7 of the 25 captions - Figures 12 and 14 and the four value grids - and only ever as a parenthesised or trailing unit inside a prose list ('20m=s', '41:67km=h', 'Power_c(dBW)'), never as a bracketed unit after the plotted quantity, so a reader who wants the unit of Figure 5's reflectance has to go to the axis [caption.units].

No caption in the paper concludes anything: none of the 25 states a result, a comparison or a direction of change, and the four that look like conclusions (the 'A show of the change of ...' family) stop at naming the two quantities being plotted [caption.concludes].

Every one of the seven grids is booktabs - a top rule, one rule under the header band and a bottom rule, with no vertical rule at any cell boundary and no box - which makes this the cleanest table set in the batch after three papers of fully ruled grids [table.rule_style].

No grid in the paper shades a row, merges a cell, prints a diagonal header, continues across a page break or carries a note row: the only structural variation among the seven is Table 2's second header band and Table 4's two abutting blocks [table.zebra].

Units go into the header or the stub on every grid that has them - dBw, km, MHz, m^-3, hour - so no cell ever repeats a unit, and the two grids whose cells are pure numbers (Tables 4 and 6) are exactly the two whose headers carry the unit instead [table.units_in_header].

Decimal alignment happens only where a column is printed to a fixed number of places: Tables 3 and 6 align because all their values carry three and two decimals, and Tables 4 and 5 do not because integers or the E-notation ratio column break the stack [table.decimal_aligned].

Grid width is not a design choice here but a column count: the two-column glossary and the five-column grids all run the full measure, and the only narrowing is whatever the tabulation engine produced [table.width].

Drawing language is one engine: 15 of the 18 figure rows are line plots from the same MATLAB export - joined traces with no markers, a key inside the top-right corner and no annotated data - while the other three are hand-drawn ray schematics with no axes at all [geometry.family].

Nothing in the paper is three-dimensional and nothing carries a colour scale: every plot is a flat 2-D frame and the only colour anywhere encodes a curve identity, not a continuous field [geometry.colorbar].

Fourteen of the fifteen plots key their curves inside the frame at upper right, the borrowed noise figure keys its six entries below the x axis instead, and the three schematics carry no key at all - so key position is the field that separates the paper's own art from its one quotation [geometry.legend].

Panel count tracks the exhibit's job rather than its subject: 8 exhibits stand on one frame (a single curve family), 8 on two frames - side by side for a parameter sweep (Figures 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11) or stacked for the F-layer height (Figures 4 and 16) - and the 2 propagation-process exercises (Figures 12 and 15) alone get a 2x2 [geometry.panel_count].

Panels share an axis only when they plot the same variable: the 2x2 propagation grids share the x axis within each column and Figure 7's polarization pair shares its grazing angle, while every sweep pair (Figures 5, 6, 9, 11) keeps two independent x axes [geometry.shared_axes].

Exhibits are announced on their own page or one page early and never later: 17 of the 25 carry lead 0 and 7 carry lead 1, with one outlier - Figure 4, announced two pages before it prints - so the announcement follows the argument's grain rather than a fixed rule [mention.lead_pages].

Citations are formulaic to the point of vacancy: most of the 25 are reached only by 'as shown in Figure N' or 'as shown in Table N', and only Figures 1, 2, 6, 8, 13, 15, 16 and 17, plus Tables 3 and 5, get a verb that reads them [mention.style].

The appendix breaks the numbering system: its two exhibits carry no number and no caption and are announced only as 'the following figure' and 'the following table', so the paper ends with two exhibits that no number reaches [mention.first_page].

Placement follows the text that introduces it rather than the top of the page: 12 of the 25 exhibits land in the middle band and 10 in the top third, and the three foot-band cases - Figure 1, Figure 13 and Table 6 - each carry their caption as the last line on the page, so a bottom-of-page exhibit always closes its page rather than opening the next [place.page_zone].

Exhibit density follows the section kind: the model sections (3.2-3.6) hold 9 of the 18 figures, section 4 holds 3, section 6 one, sensitivity 3 and the appendix 1, so the paper front-loads its drawings into the derivation and repeats the same 2x2 grammar three sections later [place.section_kind].
